page.content:
Emeryville studio that turned computer animation into a feature-film house.

How Pixar connects

  • Character: Ed Catmull — Ed Catmull co-founded Pixar and led its studio culture.
  • Work: Toy Story — Toy Story is Pixar's first feature.
  • Creator: John Lasseter — John Lasseter shaped Pixar's early features as director and creative lead.
  • Character: Steve Jobs — Steve Jobs owned and funded Pixar from 1986 until the Disney sale.
  • Event: Disney acquisition — The 2006 acquisition made Pixar a Disney studio.
  • Character: Alvy Ray Smith — Alvy Ray Smith co-founded Pixar from the Lucasfilm computer group.
  • Work: Finding Nemo — Finding Nemo is a Pixar feature.
  • Work: Monsters, Inc. — Monsters, Inc. is a Pixar feature.
  • Work: The Incredibles — The Incredibles is a Pixar feature.
  • Work: Inside Out — Inside Out is a Pixar feature.
  • Work: Luxo Jr. — Luxo Jr. is the short that became Pixar's mark.
  • Technology: RenderMan — RenderMan is Pixar's rendering technology.
  • Location: Pixar campus — The Emeryville campus is Pixar's home.
  • Work: Soul — Soul is a Pixar feature.
  • Work: WALL-E — WALL-E is a Pixar feature.
  • Faction: Pixar Braintrust — The Braintrust is Pixar's internal story-review circle.

What is Pixar?

Pixar is the studio John Lasseter, Ed Catmull, and Alvy Ray Smith built from Lucasfilm's computer division, later backed by Steve Jobs, then acquired by Disney in 2006. Its lore runs through RenderMan, the Braintrust, the Emeryville campus, and films from Toy Story to Soul.

Key threads lead to Ed Catmull, Toy Story, John Lasseter, Steve Jobs, Disney acquisition and Alvy Ray Smith.
